question: Na Slovensku im bežne hovoríme „čínske polievky“. V ktorej krajine však instantné rezance v skutočnosti vymysleli?
source_excerpt: Marketed on 25 August 1958 as Chikin Ramen

extra.why_interesting: Slovaks routinely call instant noodle soups 'čínske polievky', so the name itself points the player to China. The real answer is Japan, which turns an everyday nickname into a small 'huh, really?' moment. The player can still get there by reasoning that ramen is a Japanese word.
extra.verification_notes: Instant noodles were invented by Momofuku Ando in Japan (Nissin, 1958); the Taiwanese origin claim is marginal. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instant_noodles

explanation: Vymyslel ich Momofuku Ando, ktorý ich doma v kôlni vyvíjal pre firmu Nissin. Japonci ich v ankete dokonca vyhlásili za najlepší japonský vynález 20. storočia, pred karaoke aj walkmanom.

question: Väčšinu instantných rezancov vo fabrike najprv podusia na pare. Čo s nimi urobia potom, aby im doma stačili na prípravu tri minúty?
source_excerpt: Process for the preparation of instant fried noodles

extra.why_interesting: Players assume instant noodles are simply dried pasta. Few realise the block was deep-fried in oil, which explains both the 3-minute cooking time and the surprisingly high fat content on the label.
extra.verification_notes: Most instant noodles are steamed and then fried in oil; air-drying is the minority alternative, so the 'most' wording holds (https://patents.google.com/patent/EP0754409B1/index.php).

explanation: Prudké vysmaženie z nich vyženie vodu a zanechá drobné póry, do ktorých horúca voda rýchlo nasiakne. Preto má jedna kocka rezancov často aj vyše 15 gramov tuku.
